Looking at the z-index values for the two overlapping elements:

- `root>low>inner` has `z-index: 999`
- `root>high` has `z-index: 2`

In CSS stacking context, higher z-index values place elements on top of lower z-index values. Since 999 is significantly higher than 2, the `root>low>inner` element will be rendered above `root>high` in the overlapping region.

Both elements are positioned absolutely within the same stacking context (the root), so their z-index values directly determine their stacking order.

ANSWER: root>low>inner
